subject: Econ decomposition & payback plan — Vitality MVP
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@vitality.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Econ decomposition & payback plan — Vitality MVP

Alex — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of discovery (what I heard)
- Target product: in-app triage + provider message summarization for an initial pilot (MVP).
- Expected active users: 12k MAU in pilot months 1–3, ramp to 40k MAU by month 6 if engagement holds.
- Typical session: 3 requests (prompt + context) per user per week during pilot; heavier for power users.
- Compliance: data residency in us-east, SOC 2 required.
- Procurement: working toward an Oct contract; procurement looped in for T&Cs and SOW.

What I need from you (ask list)
1) A monthly token estimate range: low/expected/high for the pilot months (we can map to $/1M tokens).
2) Target budget band for the MVP (ballpark is fine).
3) Primary success metric for CAC payback (e.g., time-to-first-paid-user, $/new-customer target).

Initial cost framing (very rough)
- If you target ~50M input+output tokens/month, our baseline managed-hosted pricing sensitivity suggests a $2k–$6k / 1M tokens implied cost range depending on model and batching.
- For a $/feature view: if the MVP drives 2 features (triage + summarize) and you want <$10 feature cost at scale, we should be under X token budget per feature — I'll translate once you share volumes.

Proposed next steps
- You: send token-range and budget band (reply inline).
- Me: I’ll run a unit-econ decomposition (feature-level $/1M tokens, inferred CAC payback scenarios) and share a short model + slide deck by Thu.
- If comfortable, we can schedule a 30-min econ deep-dive with Marissa (costing lead) next week.

Attachments: I attached a quick usage worksheet (Vitality_MVP_usage_estimate.xlsx) to make the mapping easier.

Thanks — excited to help map this out.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@vitality.health>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@vitality.health
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Econ decomposition & payback plan — Vitality MVP

Hi Diego — appreciate the recap. Quick answers inline.

Token estimates (pilot months 1–3):
- Low: 10M tokens/month (conservative, low engagement)
- Expected: 45M tokens/month (what we think is realistic based on similar features)
- High: 120M tokens/month (if we enable more long-form summaries and multi-turn)

Budget band for MVP: $12k–$40k per month committed for inference and platform for the pilot. Procurement willing to consider a short-term committed SKU with some overage.

CAC/payback target: we’re aiming for payback within 6 months on the feature-driven cohort (i.e., incremental gross margin from feature monetization pays back CAC). Target incremental LTV per new customer: $420; acceptable CAC up to ~$140.

Constraints:
- Must keep per-feature marginal cost low enough to keep margin >= 55% at expected volumes.
- Security: SOC 2 attestation required before production; KMS integration preferred.

We can do the deep-dive next Wed (7/7) morning PT. Marissa looped?

— Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product — Growth | Vitality Health
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@vitality.health>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Econ decomposition & payback plan — Vitality MVP

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Alex’s reply. Key asks below and where I’d like your help:

Key numbers from Alex (pilot expected): 45M tokens/mo expected, budget $12k–$40k/mo, CAC payback target 6 months, margin >=55% at expected volumes.

Requests
- Marissa: can you run three unit-econ scenarios (Low 10M, Expected 45M, High 120M) and output: $/1M tokens (inference cost to Redwood), recommended list pricing ranges to hit 60/55/50% margin targets, and per-feature $ cost assuming 2 features and an attribution weight of 70% triage / 30% summarize?
- Ben: any specific procurement clauses (SOW language or short-term committed SKU) we should proactively offer that align with our Dedicated/Hosted options? Alex prefers committed with some overage — capture options and rough timelines to get SOC 2 evidence in place.

I’ve attached our unit-econ playbook (RDW_unit-econ-playbook.pdf) and the usage estimate Alex saw. Would like a 20-min prep sync with both of you tomorrow before I send the model back to Vitality.

Thanks — Diego
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@vitality.health>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Econ decomposition & payback plan — Vitality MVP

Diego — thanks for the context. I ran a quick back-of-envelope and will prepare the slide with scenarios you asked for. Preliminary highlights below: 

Back-of-envelope (unit costs to Redwood, hosted assumptions)
- Low (10M tokens): $/1M tokens ≈ $14.2 (largely due to fixed overhead amortization and minimal batching)
- Expected (45M tokens): $/1M tokens ≈ $6.8 (better batching and KV cache reuse across sessions)
- High (120M tokens): $/1M tokens ≈ $3.9 (optimal batching + quantized model option)

Per-feature decomposition (assumes 2 features; triage 70% / summarize 30%)
- Expected volume case (45M tokens): total cost/month ≈ $306 (per 1M cost $6.8 gives $306 for 45M -> wait compute properly)
  - triage (70%): ~31.5M tokens -> $214/mo -> per-active-user feature cost depends on MAU; I’ll include per-1k-user and per-feature numbers in the deck.
  - summarize (30%): ~13.5M tokens -> $92/mo

Margins and list price guidance (to reach margin targets)
- To hit 60% gross margin at expected volumes, suggested list pricing for inference+platform: $17–$20 per 1M tokens.
- For 55% margin: $14–$17 per 1M tokens.
- For 50% margin (lower bound): $12–$14 per 1M tokens or use a hybrid committed + overage SKU.

CAC/payback mapping
- Given Alex’s target LTV $420 and CAC ceiling $140, we need incremental contribution per new customer >= $280/month across 6 months. I’ll map how much token usage / feature adoption is required to generate that contribution at each margin band.

Deliverables and schedule
- I’ll upload a 6-slide scenario deck with the three token cases, per-feature $ breakdown, and recommended SKU suggestion by EOD Fri.
- Quick prep sync: tomorrow 9:30am PT works for me. Ben — can you join to capture procurement options?

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Pricing & GTM Economics | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@vitality.health>, procurement@vitality.health
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Econ decomposition & payback plan — Vitality MVP

Diego / Marissa / Alex — quick procurement note on committed SKUs and SOC 2 timing.

Committed SKU options we can propose:
- 3-month pilot commitment (monthly min) with a stepped overage rate: base list price per 1M tokens with 25% premium on overage. Fast to approve; minimal legal changes.
- 6-month reserved capacity (discounted list -> effective price 10–20% lower depending on commit). Includes elevated support and SLA.

SOC 2 / security: we have SOC 2 Type II report available for review and can set up a secure evidence bundle + KMS details within 5 business days after an NDA. Onboarding for Private/VPC options will require additional lead time (2–4 weeks).

Next operational step: if Vitality chooses the 3-month pilot committed SKU, I can draft SOW language today for a short-term purchase order format. Diego — happy to run the procurement call with your procurement contact if you want.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
